question: Should OpenClaw accept a new public operator-admin Gateway RPC, `agents.setDefault`, for changing the default agent, or should clients continue using the existing config write APIs?
rationale: Source inspection proves the method is missing, but adding a Gateway/protocol/SDK/Admin HTTP write method creates a public API contract and new operator action that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor `agents.setDefault`
options.body: Accept the dedicated RPC as an additive agent-management API and ask for a focused implementation with compatibility and proof across protocol, SDK, Admin HTTP, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep config writes only
options.body: Decline the new method and tell desktop or web clients to continue using `config.set` or `config.patch` against the canonical `agents.list[].default` shape.

options.title: Defer agent API design
options.body: Keep the request open but block implementation until maintainers choose a broader agent-management mutation strategy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor `agents.setDefault`
recommendation.body: Accept the dedicated RPC as an additive agent-management API and ask for a focused implementation with compatibility and proof across protocol, SDK, Admin HTTP, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the sibling Gateway agent CRUD API family, so they are the best available routing owner for whether this method belongs with that family.
